messages.subject: Re: Simple DLM in NIMBLE
messages.body_plain:
Hi Perry,

Thanks for you reply, and for the clarification about how NIMBLE uses rows to denote a whole set of states from time T=1....N.  That illuminates additional problems I was encountering when trying to loop over a ModelValues object as you might with a list.  This makes me think my previous step might also not be perfectly congruous with NIMBLE ModelValue Objects.  Before I copy the states into the model, I have a function that performs FFBS to generate states from time T=0...365.

As you can see in the code below, I am creating a model values object and then storing generated states in mvTheta as I loop over the time points.  I see now with NIMBLE this creates a ModelValues object of size 366. What I would like to do is then copy those 365 state variables (dropping the initial state 0) to a model object.  As you point out, however, when I run this code I only copy the first row of mvTheta rather than the whole set of 365.

Do you think the best way to handle this is to loop over the Model Values object in the copy statement or somehow store all 365 states into a size 1 ModelValues object in my FFBS step? Sorry for the long post. If it would be helpful to attach my full R script, please me me know.

Thanks again for you assistance,

Colin

modvals = modelValues(smosModel, m = 1)

nimCopy(from=test2$mvTheta,to=modvals,nodes='theta',nodesTo='x',row=1)

FFBStep<-nimbleFunction(
  setup=function(model,mvKF,nodes){
    mvThetaConfig <- modelValuesConf(vars = c('ht', 'Ht', 'theta'),types=c('double','double','double'), sizes=list(ht = 2, Ht = c(2, 2), theta = c(1,2)))
    mvTheta <- modelValues(mvThetaConfig)
    nodes <- model$expandNodeNames(nodes,sort=TRUE)
    timePoints <- length(nodes)
    len <- timePoints+1
  },
  run=function(){
    resize(mvTheta,timePoints+1)
    #Simulate Theta T
    Cho_T<-chol(mvKF['Ct',timePoints+1])
    mvTheta['theta',timePoints+1] <<- rmnorm_chol(n=1,mvKF['mt',timePoints+1],Cho_T,prec_param = FALSE)
    for (t in 1:365){
      mvTheta['ht',len-t] <<- mvKF['mt',len-t]+mvKF['Ct',len-t]%*%t(model$G)%*%inverse(mvKF['Rt',len-t+1])%*%mvTheta['theta',len-t+1]-mvKF['at',len-t+1]
      mvTheta['Ht',len-t] <<- mvKF['Ct',len-t]-mvKF['Ct',len-t]%*%t(model$G)%*%inverse(mvKF['Rt',len-t+1])%*%(model$G)%*%mvKF['Ct',len-t]
      Chold <- mvTheta['Ht',len-t]
      mvTheta['theta',len-t] <<- rmnorm_chol(n=1,mvTheta['ht',len-t],Chold,prec_param = FALSE)
    }
  }
)

I think I see what you are saying.

Although the way you’ve done it does flip the concepts a bit, it seems reasonable and valid.  (A related design issue for NIMBLE is when and how it would be useful to make a program work across many nodes that follow the same motif, such as many latent states in a state-space model, as opposed to always treating each node as distinct.  Thoughts welcome.)

I think an alternative would be the following.  If I follow, ht is a 2x365 (or 365x2) matrix.

You could assign into pieces of it using
mvTheta[‘ht’,1][1:2, i] <- (…)

and so on for the other variables.

In a sense what I think you need here is a data structure that can hold ht, Ht and theta the way an R list would, rather than necessarily a modelValues object.  Such data structures will be in NIMBLE soon.

Also I note that the argument chold to rmnorm_chol should be a Cholesky matrix.

Perry

messages.subject: Fitting a basic 2-state HMM
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm just getting started out with NIMBLE and am trying to get a 2-state HMM (with gamma state-dependent densities) up and running. I would like to eventually fit a more complex model using MCEM.

So far, I can not get the nimbleModel to run without errors. Right now, I am seeing the following error:

> Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data, inits, check = FALSE, dimensions=list(T=c(2,2)))
defining model...
Detected phi as data within 'constants'.
Error in genVarInfo3() :
  There is a problem with some indexing in this line: p <- T[theta[i_minus_1], 1:2].
One way this can happen is if you wanted to provide a vector of indices but did not include it in constants.

And here's all of the code I am running (or rather attempting to run):

## define HMM
code <- nimbleCode({

  a[1] ~ dnorm(-2, 1)
  gam[1] <- exp(a[1])/(1+exp(a[1]))
  a[2] ~ dnorm(-2, 1)
  gam[2] <- exp(a[2])/(1+exp(a[2]))

  T[1,1] <- 1-gam[1]
  T[2,1] <- gam[2]
  T[1,2] <- gam[1]
  T[2,2] <- 1-gam[2]

  phi <- c(.5, .5)
  theta[1] ~ dcat(prob = phi)

  for(i in 2:k) {
    p <- T[theta[i-1],]
    theta[i] ~ dcat(prob = p)
  }

  for (i in 1:k) {
    y[i] ~ dgamma(shape=alp[theta[i]], rate=bet[theta[i]])
  }

  for(i in 1:2){
    alp[i] ~ dgamma(1,1)
    bet[i] ~ dgamma(1,1)
  }

})

y <- rgamma(100, 1, 1)
k <- 100

alp <- numeric(2)
bet <- numeric(2)

## define model constants, data, and initial values
constants <- list(k=k, phi=c(1/2,1/2))
data <- list(y = y)
inits <- list(theta=sample(x=c(1,2), size = 100, replace = T), a = rep(-2,2),
              alp=c(1,1), bet=c(1,1))

## create model object
Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data, inits, check = FALSE, dimensions=list(T=c(2,2)))

If anyone could point me in the right direction, it'd be much appreciated! I have also tried to go through the R code from the Efficient MCMC Sampling for HHMMs paper but am not familiar with most of the models used in capture-recapture.

Thank you,

Vianey

Vianey, this approach I'm going to suggest is not the most computationally efficient, but it does work.

Until we implement stochastic indexing (e.g., being able to index alp[] using the stochastic index theta[i], you can side-step the issue using:

for (i in 1:k) {

    shape_param[i] <- equals(theta[i],1)*alp[1] + equals(theta[i],2)*alp[2]
    rate_param[i]  <- equals(theta[i],1)*bet[1] + equals(theta[i],2)*bet[2]
    y[i] ~ dgamma(shape=shape_param[i], rate=rate_param[i])
}

Daniel

Hi Perry,

Thanks for your suggestion, and I'm glad to hear a NIMBLE version of List is in the works.   What I ended up doing is in the modelValuesConf, define the size of theta = c(2,366).  Then as you suggest, just update the first row, and leave the other 365 rows empty.  Note: had to resize the modelValues object to 366 rows to store the other values, ht (2x1) and Ht, which is a 2x2 matrix.

Copying over the values of theta seems to work great using the code below.  One more quick question about how NIMBLE works is in regards to the copying.  The modelValues object is 2 x 365 because there is an initial state X0, which is its own variable.  However, the theta ModelValues object has 366 columns.  When I do the copying NIMBLE seems to automatically resize the modvals object and copies all 366 states.  Is there a way to drop the first state in the copying process?  Something akin to how in R you can put mvTheta[,-1] to drop the first column?

Thanks again,

Colin

           modvals = modelValues(smosModel, m = 1)
> nimCopy(from=test2$mvTheta,to=modvals,nodes='theta',nodesTo='x',row=1)

FFBStep<-nimbleFunction(
  setup=function(model,mvKF,nodes){
    mvThetaConfig <- modelValuesConf(vars = c('ht', 'Ht', 'theta'),types=c('double','double','double'), sizes=list(ht = 2, Ht = c(2, 2), theta=c(2,366)))

    mvTheta <- modelValues(mvThetaConfig)
    nodes <- model$expandNodeNames(nodes,sort=TRUE)
    timePoints <- length(nodes)
    len <- timePoints+1
  },
  run=function(){
    resize(mvTheta,timePoints+1)
    #Simulate Theta T
    Cho_T<-chol(mvKF['Ct',timePoints+1])

    mvTheta['theta',1][1:2,timePoints+1] <<- rmnorm_chol(n=1,mvKF['mt',timePoints+1],Cho_T,prec_param = FALSE)

    for (t in 1:365){

      mvTheta['ht',len-t] <<- mvKF['mt',len-t]+mvKF['Ct',len-t]%*%t(model$G)%*%inverse(mvKF['Rt',len-t+1])%*%mvTheta['theta',1][1:2,len-t+1]-mvKF['at',len-t+1]

      mvTheta['Ht',len-t] <<- mvKF['Ct',len-t]-mvKF['Ct',len-t]%*%t(model$G)%*%inverse(mvKF['Rt',len-t+1])%*%(model$G)%*%mvKF['Ct',len-t]

      Chold <- chol(mvTheta['Ht',len-t])
      mvTheta['theta',1][1:2,len-t] <<- rmnorm_chol(n=1,mvTheta['ht',len-t],Chold,prec_param = FALSE)
    }
  }
)

You should be able to say

model[[‘theta’]][1:2, 2:366] <<- mvTheta[1, ‘x’][1:2, 1:365]

Perry

You should be able to say

nimCopy(…, nodes = ‘theta[1:2, 2:366]’, nodesTo = ‘x[1:2, 1:365]’, row = 1)

Is that what you need?

Also nimCopy is most useful when there are nodes from multiple variables

> You should be able to say

> >
> > Copying over the values of theta seems to work great using the code below.  One more quick question about how NIMBLE works is in regards to the copying.  The modelValues object is 2 x 365 because there is an initial state X0, which is its own variable.  However, the theta ModelValues object has 366 columns.  When I do the copying NIMBLE seems to automatically resize the modvals object and copies all 366 states.  Is there a way to drop the first state in the copying process? > >

> >     len <- timePoints+1
> >   },

> >       mvTheta['theta',1][1:2,len-t] <<- rmnorm_chol(n=1,mvTheta['ht',len-t],Chold,prec_param = FALSE)

> >   }
> > )
> >
> >
> > On Thursday, December 1, 2016 at 11:08:50 AM UTC-6, nimble.stats wrote:
> > > I think I see what you are saying.
> > >
> > > Although the way you’ve done it does flip the concepts a bit, it seems reasonable and valid.  (A related design issue for NIMBLE is when and how it would be useful to make a program work across many nodes that follow the same motif, such as many latent states in a state-space model, as opposed to always treating each node as distinct.  Thoughts welcome.)
> > >
> > > I think an alternative would be the following.  If I follow, ht is a 2x365 (or 365x2) matrix.
> > >
> > > You could assign into pieces of it using

> > > >       mvTheta['Ht',len-t] <<- mvKF['Ct',len-t]-mvKF['Ct',len-t]%*%t(model$G)%*%inverse(mvKF['Rt',len-t+1])%*%(model$G)%*%mvKF['Ct',len-t]
> > > >       Chold <- mvTheta['Ht',len-t]

What we mean is a complete set of states, not a row of a particular variable in nimble that might happen to be a matrix.  For modelValues purposes, you can think of all model variables as being flattened, like having their dimension attribute removed in R.

> > > > > > Hi Daniel,

> > > > > > I have a quick follow up question about the best way to set up the latent nodes in a NIMBLE model step.  I am at the point where I am trying to use NimCopy to copy over simulated nodes from a ModelValues object to the model.  It looks like NIMBLE only allows you to copy by row. > > > > > >

> > > > > >
> > > > > > This creates an issue when I create a modelValues object, e.g.,  modvals = modelValues(smosModel, m = 1) as it creates a 2 x 365 matrix, so you can't iterate over rows when running NimCopy. messages.subject: Custom Sampler and mvSaved
messages.body_plain:
Dear Nimble Users,

I am writing my own sampler and have a question about mvSaved.  My understanding is mvSaved stores every iteration of the targets and/or nodes of the MCMC sampler.  However, after running the sampler it seems to only store the final iteration.   In my example below, the targets are getting saved in mvSamples, but I am unable to find a place where each iteration of the latent nodes are stored.  My first solution was to add monitors to the MCMC object, but I received an error warning:   ‘addMonitors’ is not a valid field or method name for reference class “nfRefClass_nimble33”  Maybe this is the wrong approach?

Below is my code for the sampler, and I am attaching a full version with simulated data.

I am just curious if I need to add another line or command to save both the targets and latent states for each iteration of the sampler.

Any information or suggestions would be much appreciated.

Thanks,

Colin

sampler_Kalman <- nimbleFunction(
  contains = sampler_BASE,
  setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {

    ## set up numeric values

    T <- length(model$x[1,])
    T2 <- ctmiss(model$y)
    a1 <- model$getParam('sigmaSquaredInvv', 'shape')
    a2 <- model$getParam('sigmaSquaredInvw', 'shape')
    b1 <- model$getParam('sigmaSquaredInvv', 'rate')
    b2 <- model$getParam('sigmaSquaredInvw', 'rate')
    sh1 <- a1+T2/2      #Posterior V shape, fixed bc conjugacy
    sh2 <- a2+(T*2)/2   #Posterior W shape, fixed bc conjugacy

    ## functions for kalman, ffbs, sse
    filt <- KalmanStep(model,'x')
    level <- FFBStep(model,filt$mvKF,'x')
    y_sse <- see_y(model,level$mvTheta)
    theta_sse <- see_st(model,level$mvTheta)
  },
  run = function() {
    filt$run()
    level$run()

    #draw observation for precision 1, V
    rate <- b1 + y_sse$run()/2
    psi1 <- rgamma(1, sh1, rate=rate)

    #draw observation for precision 2, W
    rate <- b2 + theta_sse$run()/2
    psi2 <- rgamma(1, sh2, rate=rate)

    #Update model variance terms
    model[[target[1]]] <<- psi1
    model[[target[2]]] <<- psi2

    #Update Latent States in Model; I think this means I only need initialization step once?
    nimCopy(from=level$mvTheta,to=model,nodes='theta[1:2,2:366]',nodesTo='x[1:2,1:365]',row=1)

    #model$calculate(dependnecies of latent nodes)

    #Save states and variance terms to mvSaved
    nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, nodes='x', row = 1)
    nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, nodes = target, row=1)

  },
  methods = list(
    reset = function () {}
  )
)

#Run Sampler
smosSpec <- configureMCMC(smosModel, print = TRUE)
smosSpec$removeSamplers(c('x','sigmaSquaredInvv', 'sigmaSquaredInvw'),print = FALSE)
smosSpec$addSampler(target = c('sigmaSquaredInvv','sigmaSquaredInvw'), type = 'sampler_Kalman')
smosMCMC <- buildMCMC(smosSpec)

#Run MCMC for 10 iterations

smosMCMC$run(10)

messages.subject: Re: Custom Sampler and mvSaved
messages.body_plain:
Hi Colin,

The job of mvSaved is only to store the current state of the model, not the outputs from the chain.  Each sampler does not have to worry about storing outputs, only about ensuring that mvSaved is up to date when it exits.  The “MCMC” object created by buildMCMC, which manages execution of all the samplers, will manage storage of outputs in mvSamples. A sampler can assume that upon entry mvSaved has the same values for model variables and associated log probabilities as the model itself.  Upon exit the sampler must ensure that is again the case.  Hence if it has modified values in the model (by a proposal and some calculations), then if it accepts the proposal, it needs to copy from the model to mvSaved, but if it rejects the proposal, it needs to copy from mvSaved to the model.  The avoids needing to recalculate parts of the model simply to get it back into the correct state after rejecting a proposal.

The step for adding monitors is to the the configuration (the smosSpec in your code), not the built MCMC (smosMCMC in your code).

Let me know if anything doesn’t make sense.

Perry

Ah, Chris’ email made me realize that when I responded to Jose I neglected to cc nimble-users!  In case others are interested, here was my answer.  Jose did report to me that clearCompiled() crashed Windows but not OS X.  -Perry

This has been a headache for us.  If you are running in Linux or OS X, you can use what is still an internal/development feature:

nimble:::clearCompiled(Rmodel)

where Rmodel is any part (model or nimbleFunction) of a nimble project (stuff that was compiled together, perhaps via the project argument to compileNimble).   This is not fully documented for users for a few reasons.  One is that it is new.  Another is that it doesn’t work safely on Windows.  And a third is that one still has to be careful: we’ve tried to make it completely safe but it is not fully tested.  In particular it is possible that if you have multiple R objects of the same nimble object, and you accidentally try to use one of them later, the system could crash.  It shouldn’t happen, but as mentioned it is not highly tested.  But for your purposes if you are writing a loop in which you compile and then want to clear at the end, go ahead and try it and it is likely to work.  Unfortunately Windows manages compiled and loaded stuff differently.  On Windows, in some cases what might happen is that the compiled objects will unload but the non-safeness will mean that R crashes upon exiting.  If you can live with that you can use it.  In any case it won’t cause harm to try it as long as you know it might be unstable and don’t have unsaved work in the R session.

  contains = sampler_BASE,

messages.body_plain:
Hi Colin,

I am not sure what’s going wrong, so I can just give some speculation and suggestions.

It looks like a1, a2, b1 and b2 are constants in the model, since they are set once in setup code and not again.  That would mean the model must be initialized with those values when the MCMC is built.  It sounds like that is not the problem but worth double-checking.

The way you are using mvTheta to share variables among several nimbleFunctions should work.  We had a related bug recently (but not for modelValues) that made me double check if your arrangements work and they seem to be ok as far as I could check.  By the way, below I suggest a couple of different ways you could accomplish the sharing of theta.  Use of nimCopy will be less efficient than a direct copy if it is just for one variable (theta).

A good way to check what is going on during compiled execution is with print.  e.g. print(mvThetaS[’theta’,1])

One concern is I don’t see where you are keeping mvSaved up to date. The rule is that you can assume mvSaved is fully sync’ed with the model upon entry and you must ensure that is again the case upon exit.  So usually there is a nimCopy near the end of a sampler to update mvSaved (for an accepted move) or from mvSaved to the model (for a rejected move).  I guess you could be doing that in y_sse or theta_sse, but then it is suspicious that you are doing model$calculate after calling those functions.  model$calculate will update the state of log probabilities and deterministic nodes in the model, so it is suspicious to see it as the last thing done in a sampler.  That means it will put the model out of sync with mvSaved.

Also I assume you are sure that calculating the nodes and then the dependencies of target provides a correct ordering based on the model structure.  To be more generic you could create one topologically sorted vector of nodes with model$topologicallySortNodes(c(nodes, paramDependencies)).   Or I wonder if model$getDependencies(c(target, ‘x’)) would be correct (but potentially different from what you have)?

Here are two other possible ways to arrange for nimbleFunctions to share variables:

##method 1: In compiled execution, numeric objects are passed by reference.  This makes behavior different from uncompiled execution.
nf1 <- nimbleFunction(
    setup = function() {
        sharedX <- as.numeric(1:5)
        mynf2 <- nf2()
    },
    run = function() {
        print(sharedX)
        mynf2$run(sharedX) ## if setup code is needed. could also give a return value.
        print(sharedX)
        nf3(sharedX)       ## if setup code is not needed. ditto.
        print(sharedX)
    })

nf2 <- nimbleFunction(
    setup = function() {},
    run = function(x = double(1)) { ## x will be passed by reference
        x <- x * 2
    })

nf3 <- nimbleFunction(
    run = function(x = double(1)) { ## x will be passed by reference
        x <- x + 100
    })

mynf1 <- nf1()
mynf1$run() ## passed by copy in uncompiled execution

cmynf1 <- compileNimble(mynf1)
cmynf1$run() ## passed by reference in compiled execution

## method 2: use a nimbleFunction with no functions as a data structure ( section 9.5.19 of user manual ).
nf1 <- nimbleFunction(
    setup = function() {
        myDataNF <- dataNF()
        initX <- as.numeric(1:2)
        mynf2 <- nf2(myDataNF)
    },
    run = function() {
        myDataNF$sharedX <- initX
        print(myDataNF$sharedX)
        mynf2$run()  ## could give a return value as well as modifying sharedX
        print(myDataNF$sharedX)
    })

nf2 <- nimbleFunction(
    setup = function(myDataNF) {},
    run = function() {
        myDataNF$sharedX <<- myDataNF$sharedX * 2
    })

dataNF <- nimbleFunction(
    setup = function() {
        sharedX <- numeric(2) ## make sure nimble knows it's a vector
        setupOutputs(sharedX) ## ensure it is preserved through compilation since it doesn’t appear in methods
    })

mynf1 <- nf1()
mynf1$run()
cmynf1 <- compileNimble(mynf1)
cmynf1$run()

Hope that helps.
Perry
